events.title: Dangote Refinery share offer (IPO)
events.summary: The refinery is selling shares to the public for the first time — the first refinery ever offered on the Nigerian Exchange. Buying shares makes you part-owner of the business, so what you get back depends on how it performs. Unlike a bond, nothing is guaranteed.
events.minimum: 10 shares — ₦5,250
events.tenor: No end date — you hold the shares until you sell them
howTo: Applications close on Tuesday 13 October — this is the last week
You need a CSCS account, which your broker or investment app opens for you
Subscribe through NGX Invest, a licensed stockbroker, or an SEC-registered investment app
Check any platform on the SEC register at sec.gov.ng before you send money
If the offer is oversubscribed you receive fewer shares than you applied for, and the rest is refunded
Allotment and the listing date follow the timetable in the prospectus, and are announced after the close

events.title: FGN Savings Bond — October offer
events.summary: The monthly retail window. The 3-year pays 14.071% and the 2-year 13.071% — on ₦100,000 at the 3-year rate that is ₦3,518 into your account every three months for three years, then your ₦100,000 back. Rates are down from 15.12% in September.
events.tenor: 2 years to 14 Oct 2028, or 3 years to 14 Oct 2029
howTo: Subscriptions close on Friday 9 October — settlement follows on 14 October
Contact a DMO-appointed stockbroker, your bank’s investment desk, or an investment app today
You need a bank account in your own name, your BVN and a valid ID
Units are ₦1,000 each: minimum ₦5,000, then in multiples of ₦1,000
Interest is paid every 14 January, April, July and October

events.title: Treasury Bill auction — 7 October
events.summary: The first auction of the fourth quarter: ₦900bn offered across 91, 182 and 364-day bills, settling on 8 October. You are not paid interest on a bill — you buy it for less than it repays, and the gap is your return, less 10% withholding tax.
events.rate: Set at auction — the 364-day bill last cleared at 15.89% on 23 September
events.minimum: ₦50,000,000 at the auction · from about ₦100,000 through a bank or broker
howTo: The auction itself is for large institutions. To buy a smaller parcel, ask your bank’s treasury desk or a stockbroker
Ask what rate they are offering and compare it with the auction rate — the gap is their margin
Since October 2025, 10% withholding tax is deducted from the return on Treasury Bills. FGN bonds are still exempt
Your money itself is returned in full at maturity

events.title: FGN Bond auction — October
events.summary: The government’s main monthly borrowing, in bonds lasting ten years or more. The minimum at the auction itself is ₦50 million, so this is not where most people buy — but the rate set here is the anchor every other rate follows, and you can buy the same bonds in small amounts afterwards through a broker.
events.rate: Set at auction — September’s new 10-year cleared at 16.79%
events.minimum: ₦50,000,000 at the auction · from about ₦10,000 through a broker afterwards
howTo: Most people do not bid here. Watch the rate instead: it tells you where all other rates are heading
To own these bonds in a smaller amount, ask a stockbroker about buying on the secondary market
The DMO publishes the offer circular about a week before the auction
events.expectedNote: The DMO holds one FGN Bond auction a month; September’s was on Monday the 14th, settling on the 16th. The Q4 2026 issuance calendar had not been published when this was checked.

events.title: NBS inflation figures — September data
events.summary: The official measure of how fast prices are rising. This is the number your investments have to beat just to keep your money from shrinking.
events.expectedNote: The NBS releases each month CPI on the 15th of the following month, or the next working day.

A 364-day bill clearing at 15.89%, September’s rate, means paying about ₦86,300 today for ₦100,000 in a year — the ₦13,700 gap is your return, less 10% withholding tax.
